title: Migration workshop: OpenAI/Anthropic/Together -> Redwood API (console + Optimize walkthrough)
summary: Redwood AE/SE walked Darkwater through a migration playbook for swapping OpenAI/Anthropic/Together endpoints to the Redwood API. Covered request/response parity, streaming and function-call differences, console rollout controls, Optimize heuristics for batching/quantization, and private deployment security (KMS + SSO). Customer expressed cost/latency sensitivity and regulatory concerns; agreed to a 4-week POC with benchmarks and a security packet review.
transcript:
Meeting title: Migration workshop: OpenAI/Anthropic/Together -> Redwood API (console + Optimize walkthrough)
Date/Time: 2026-11-29 15:00 PST
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Lina Gomez (Redwood Product), Evan Shaw (Darkwater CTO), Priya Narang (ML Eng Lead), Marcus Li (Infra), Sophie Tran (Procurement)

--- Auto-generated summary (may be partial) ---
Redwood walked through parity mapping and console ops; customer asked about VPC/KMS and SSO; next steps: send security docs, pricing, sample mapping spreadsheet, schedule POC kickoff.

--- Transcript ---
0:00 - Maya Chen: okay folks let's kick off, thanks for making time. um quick around the room, i'm maya from redwood and ravi will do the technical deep dive later, lina on product.
0:10 - Evan Shaw: yeah thanks, tough week but excited. Evan here, CTO at Darkwater. we've been evaluating migrating our inference away from the combo of OpenAI + Anthropic + Together.
0:20 - Priya Narang: Priya, ml lead; we're primarily concerned about latency and replication of existing function-calling behavior. also data residency for some PHI-like logs.
0:30 - Marcus Li: Marcus, infra; i'll ask the hard k8s and vpc questions.
0:35 - Maya Chen: great, objective for today: show how you map existing endpoints and features to the Redwood API, run through the console and Optimize suggestions, and outline a POC.
0:45 - Sophie Tran: Sophie from procurement; i'll mostly listen for contract-ish questions.
1:10 - Ravi Patel: ok jumping in, so first thing: parity mapping. i've got a short sheet showing the typical differences — request envelope, streaming, function-calls, and response heuristics. in practice, mapping is usually straightforward but there are a few gotchas.
1:35 - Ravi Patel: for example, OpenAI style function calling has a specific payload; together/together.ai has slightly different tokenization defaults and stop behavior. on redwood you can configure model profiles to mimic those behaviors — same param names or adapter layer.
1:50 - Priya Narang: adapter layer — we'd prefer to avoid a big translation shim in prod. is that a runtime cost?
2:05 - Ravi Patel: minimal if you put it as a lightweight proxy — most customers either do a 50-line adapter or use our prebuilt mapping we share as a gist. it doesn't add token cost, it's just request/response shaping.
2:25 - Evan Shaw: tokenization differences worry us; we have edge cases in our summarization where anthro/alpha tokenizer produced slightly different outputs. how do you validate equivalence?
2:45 - Lina Gomez: we recommend running a small eval harness — send your canonical prompts and compare logits/output with normalized metrics (ROUGE + business metrics). we also provide quantized model suggestions in Optimize so you can test parities at different cost points.
3:10 - Marcus Li: on infra: we need VPC and BYOK KMS. is that in private?
3:20 - Maya Chen: yes, Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM and runs in your VPC or on-prem bundle. we can scope an air-gapped option; we'll include specifics in the security packet.
3:35 - Marcus Li: and SSO — SAML?
3:38 - Maya Chen: SSO via SAML/SCIM provisioning and RBAC are standard in enterprise packages.
3:50 - Evan Shaw: what's the expected delta in latency vs OpenAI baseline? we can't add 50–100 ms per call.
4:05 - Ravi Patel: typical is within 5–20 ms for comparable hosted endpoints; if you go Dedicated with pinned GPUs you get lower jitter and predictable p99. Optimize can suggest smaller sequence-length-optimized kernels and batching configs to reduce per-token cost while keeping latencies within SLO.
4:35 - Priya Narang: can you show the console where we can inspect token-level cost per route?
4:45 - Lina Gomez: yep i'll share my screen.
4:52 - [screen share starts, noise: mouse clicks] 
5:10 - Lina Gomez: this is the Console — top-right you can filter by model, route, and token buckets. here's a sample route you can pin to a model variant. you get token burn down, p50/p95 latency, and per-request traces.
5:35 - Priya Narang: can we attach our custom evals?
5:40 - Lina Gomez: yes, under Evals you can upload prompt sets, define pass/fail thresholds, and get regression alerts when a new model or quantization profile degrades quality.
6:05 - Ravi Patel: demo note: when you run a canary rollout, traffic is split at the routing layer and we keep automatic fallback to the previous variant if errors spike or latency exceeds threshold.
6:25 - Marcus Li: is there a way to do traffic routing by header or token? we need to route internal traffic to dedicated nodes and external to hosted.
6:35 - Lina Gomez: absolutely — routing policies can be header-based, route-based, or cost-based. you can also hard-pin routes to Dedicated pools.
6:50 - Evan Shaw: what about function calling semantics — we rely on JSON-schema enforcement in the call results.
7:05 - Ravi Patel: Redwood supports structured outputs and function-call style behaviors; the only difference is you can opt into strict schema validation at the runtime and fail-fast if the model returns invalid shapes. that reduces downstream parsing logic.
7:30 - Priya Narang: perfect. any nuance with streaming + function calls? we occasionally stream partial function arguments and finish later.
7:45 - Ravi Patel: streaming supports incremental function payloads; we preserve order and partial results. small caveat: when using KV cache with streaming you may need to tune chunk sizes for very long chat histories.
8:05 - Evan Shaw: KV cache — does it leak across customers?
8:10 - Maya Chen: no, tenant isolation is enforced. for Dedicated and Private, KV stores are per-tenant and can be encrypted with your KMS.
8:20 - Sophie Tran: procurement — what's the contracting cadence for Dedicated?
8:25 - Maya Chen: Dedicated is usually committed monthly/annual capacity with an SLA. procurement we can follow up with standard T&Cs and customization.
8:40 - [short pause, typing sounds] 
9:05 - Lina Gomez: now switching to Optimize — this is where we run heuristics on your workload and suggest batching, caching, and quantization settings.
9:20 - Lina Gomez: here's an example: for your summarization pipeline we see short prompt + long completion. Optimize suggested small-batch streaming with prefix caching to reduce tokens and keep p95 under 300ms.
9:40 - Priya Narang: quantization — do you support int8 and newer 4-bit formats? how do we validate quality?
9:55 - Ravi Patel: yes, we support int8 and multiple 4-bit quant profiles; Optimize will produce a quality/cost frontier so you can pick the profile that meets your ROUGE or business thresholds. we keep the original FP model in the chain for canary compare.
10:20 - Evan Shaw: can you run a bench of our real prompts?
10:25 - Maya Chen: that's exactly what a POC will include — we run your prompt set, generate cost/latency/quality matrices, and give recommendations.
10:35 - Marcus Li: what logs do you ship back? we're sensitive about PII/PHI.
10:45 - Maya Chen: by default we do limited telemetry; for Private deployments you can disable telemetry and log only to your SIEM. we also have redact policies and ingestion hooks to strip PII before it leaves the VPC.
11:10 - Evan Shaw: good. ok can we see a concrete API parity example? perhaps a mapping from openai chat/completions to a Redwood request.
11:25 - Ravi Patel: sure — i'll paste a quick diff. (paraphrased) OpenAI: {model, messages[], temperature, functions[]} vs Redwood: {model_profile, prompt_chunks[], generation: {temp, max_tokens}, function_schema: {...}}. most customers do a trivial rename and reuse the messages->prompt_chunks adapter.
11:55 - Priya Narang: do you have an SDK to smooth that?
11:58 - Ravi Patel: yes, our SDK has shorthand methods and a tiny shim you can drop in. we can also provide a dockerized adapter if you want zero code-change for the first 2 weeks.
12:15 - Evan Shaw: docker adapter — that might fit our ops constraints. Marcus?
12:20 - Marcus Li: sounds ok but we'd like the adapter to run in our infra, not a hosted sidecar.
12:25 - Ravi Patel: that's supported; we give an image and config.
12:30 - [laughter] Ev: ok moving on, can you show the console for rollout policies?
12:40 - Lina Gomez: sure — here's a canary wizard: set percent, error thresholds, latency thresholds, and automatic rollback. you can also define tests to run during rollout — smoke tests or evals.
13:05 - Priya Narang: during rollback, are pending requests dropped or retried?
13:10 - Ravi Patel: we gracefully fallback existing requests to the previous variant, and new requests are routed accordingly — no silent drops.
13:20 - Sophie Tran: procurement question — what's the billing model for mixed hosted/dedicated usage?
13:30 - Maya Chen: we support hybrid billing: usage-based for hosted, committed spend for dedicated with overage pricing. we can provide a blended forecast in the POC.
13:45 - Evan Shaw: how long to stand up a Private instance?
13:50 - Maya Chen: typical is 4–8 weeks depending on network approvals; we can compress to 2–3 weeks for simple VPC peering.
14:10 - Marcus Li: audit logs retention? we need 7 years for some logs.
14:20 - Lina Gomez: we have configurable retention and can export to your logging sink (S3, GCS, Splunk) with lifecycle policies.
14:40 - Priya Narang: show me the tracing hooks in the Console.
14:50 - Lina Gomez: trace view here — you can see token-level timing, kernel selection, and batch composition. it's really handy for finding perf hotspots.
15:10 - Evan Shaw: ok let's talk POC scope and timeline. our desired success criteria: parity on 50 canonical prompts, p95 latency <= current baseline + 20ms, and cost per 1k tokens reduced by at least 20% or equal with improved reliability.
15:35 - Maya Chen: good concrete goals. typical POC: week 0 onboarding & security review, week 1–2 runbench with your prompt set, week 3 optimize and run canary, week 4 final report and recommendations.
15:55 - Priya Narang: instrumentation for the bench — we'll want to ingest detailed latency and quality metrics into our internal dashboards. can we push traces to our prometheus?
16:10 - Ravi Patel: yes, we can push metrics via exporters and give a raw batch export of request/response for quality evals.
16:25 - Evan Shaw: any hidden gotchas switching together-based endpoints?
16:30 - Ravi Patel: the main one is tokenization edge cases and any proprietary tokenizers -- we often port those by normalizing inputs and adding a small pre-tokenization step. otherwise it's mostly mapping.
16:45 - Sophie Tran: i'll need a procurement packet and an estimated SOW for Dedicated.
16:50 - Maya Chen: we'll send a starter SOW and pricing ranges; for Dedicated we include capacity sizing suggestions.
17:10 - [short silence, typing] 
17:30 - Lina Gomez: quick demo: Optimize suggestion card — shows cost/quality frontier, recommended quant profile, and expected latency impact. you can export suggestions to the console rollout wizard.
17:50 - Priya Narang: do you keep old model versions for audits?
17:55 - Lina Gomez: yes, model versioning and artifact retention are part of the platform. you can pin versions per route.
18:10 - Evan Shaw: data residency — we have EU-only constraints for certain routes. can you pin region?
18:20 - Maya Chen: yes region pinning and geo-routing are supported. private deployments can be colocated in your region.
18:35 - Marcus Li: what's the SLA for Dedicated?
18:40 - Maya Chen: 99.9% monthly uptime with p95 latency targets; we'll include specifics in the SOW.
18:55 - Evan Shaw: okay let's wrap with next steps.
19:05 - Maya Chen: recap: we'll send security packet (SOC2, ISO references, KMS architecture), a sample mapping spreadsheet (openai->redwood fields + sample adapter), starter SOW with pricing bands, and proposed POC dates. we'll also run a small initial bench once we get your prompt set.
19:25 - Priya Narang: can you cc the SDK and the docker adapter?
19:30 - Maya Chen: yes, SDK links and docker adapter image will be included.
19:40 - Sophie Tran: timeline for paperwork?
19:45 - Maya Chen: procurement packet and SOW within 3 business days. security packet within 5.
19:55 - Evan Shaw: great. Marcus anything else?
20:00 - Marcus Li: just that we'd like to keep the initial POC internal traffic only; no external routing until we've validated.
20:05 - Maya Chen: noted. final q: who should we schedule the kickoff with?
20:10 - Evan Shaw: assign to Priya and Marcus. Sophie will own procurement.
20:15 - Maya Chen: perfect. thanks everyone. we'll follow up with notes and artifacts.
20:25 - [call ends]

--- End of transcript ---
